objective: Hypertrophy and strength with zero spinal compression or lumbar shear.
philosophy: Train every major muscle group using rigid external back support (chest-supported benches, high-back seats) and static/isometric core bracing.

rules.name: Zero axial loading
rules.detail: No load bearing down through the spine.

rules.name: Zero lumbar flexion or shear
rules.detail: No hinging or rounding under load, and no loaded spinal flexion.

rules.name: Pelvic position control
rules.detail: Leg press depth stops at a 90 degree knee angle, to eliminate lumbar rounding (butt-wink) at the bottom.

rules.name: Support requirement
rules.detail: Upper-body pressing and pulling must use a chest-supported pad or an 80-90 degree backrest.

rules.name: Isometric core only
rules.detail: Core work is anti-extension, anti-rotation, or anti-lateral-flexion. No dynamic spinal flexion.

execution.tempoDetail: 3s eccentric lowering, 1s stretch pause, 2s concentric lift, 1s peak squeeze.
execution.warmup: 1-2 warm-up sets at 60-75% of working weight before each primary compound. Should not be fatiguing — groove the movement so the first working set is the best one.
machinePreference: Leg press: seated horizontal is preferred over 45 degree incline.
Rows: 30-45 degree incline chest-supported bench or chest-supported leverage machine, never a standing variant.

ledger.why: RDLs create high axial shear stress across the L5-S1 segment.
Easier core engagement without arching the lower back.
Removes the dynamic walking load while keeping lateral core stability.
Removes torso sway and momentum, taking stress off the lower back.
Avoids extreme spinal arching while keeping continuous cable tension.

permitted.condition: Acceptable alternative to machine chest press provided the glutes stay glued to the bench and the lower back does not hyper-arch.
